title: One decision core: what acting on a row is worth and costs, one operating point chosen from it (34.1)
request: The owner moved DCLab's focus from leakage alone to more abilities; layer 5 (decide) first. The plan (docs/guides/PHASE10_ABILITIES_PLAN.md, 34.1) asks for one decision core uniting the review budget and the stated-cost threshold, with a value per row and a capacity.
spec: DecisionSpec v1 and choose_operating_point in dclab_core/decide.py; the review budget and assess's stated-cost threshold as special cases with the same answers; the main product's objective through objective_of.
plan: read decide.py, assess._threshold and the engine's wiring
write the failing tests: special cases, per-row value, capacity, holdout
one gain per row against acting on none, ranked by score or expected gain
intervals measured for what they mean
assess's stated-cost path reads the core
register the contract and its schema

decisions.decision: One gain per row: a case acted on earns its value and avoids its miss cost; a non-case costs a false alarm; every action costs its cost
decisions.why: the review budget and the stated costs are both this formula with some terms zero, so one core gives both answers

decisions.decision: Rank by expected gain only when a value per row is given and the scores are probabilities
decisions.why: a likely small case can be worth less than a less likely large one; scores that are not probabilities cannot weigh values

decisions.decision: Two intervals: the expected value's at the share chosen, and a prediction interval for the holdout
decisions.why: measured: a 90% confidence interval held a same-sized holdout's value in about 45 of 60 seeds, as statistics says it should; each interval is now tested for what it means

decisions.decision: The engine's review path stays on review_budget until 34.4
decisions.why: moving it changes stored records; 34.4 upgrades the product's decision field and moves it then

decisions.decision: Leave the engine's review path on review_budget instead of moving it onto choose_operating_point
decisions.why: the choice is already tested to be the same; the review decision has its own record shape that the report, the claims and the page read and that old projects keep, so a move would leave every reader handling two shapes; and the two read the holdout differently (a rounded count against a threshold), so review projects' holdout numbers would change for no gain

change: dclab_core/decide.py (DecisionSpec v1, choose_operating_point, _prediction); dclab_core/assess.py (stated costs read the core); dclab_core/adapters/main_product.py (objective_of); dclab_core/adapters/conformance.py, contracts.py, schemas (the contract registered); version 0.105.0 and CHANGELOG; tests/test_core_decision_spec.py (new).

findings.defect: the plan's check that the holdout's value falls in the interval asked the wrong thing
findings.scenario: a 90% interval for the expected value held a same-sized holdout's value in 45 of 60 seeds (and 43 of 60 for review_budget's own interval)
findings.cause: a confidence interval for the average does not include a new sample's own noise; for equal sizes it holds about three times in four
findings.fix: the expected value's interval is checked against the value on a very large sample (57 of 60), and a prediction interval for the holdout is given and checked (54 of 60)
findings.impact: an interval read as a promise about the holdout would be broken one time in four
findings.open: review_budget keeps its own interval (re-chosen each draw), slightly optimistic

findings.defect: a count could cut through tied scores, then the threshold flagged the whole tie
findings.scenario: y=[1,1,0], scores [0.9,0.5,0.5], a false alarm 10, a miss 1: the old threshold 0.9 (cost 1), the new 0.5 (cost 10); on scores rounded to 0.1, 86 of 200 seeds changed
findings.cause: every count was tried, not only those that end where the score changes
findings.fix: a count may end only where the rank changes; assess takes the exact score, never the rounded one
findings.impact: a different, costlier threshold for existing projects whose models give tied scores

findings.defect: the holdout was read with a value of zero per case when its values were not passed
findings.scenario: a value per row given for the training rows, none for the holdout: its value per row fell from 11.03 to -0.47 with no warning
findings.cause: the holdout fell back to the spec's value per case, zero when a value column is used
findings.fix: a value per row needs the holdout's values too, and a value column needs its values: both refused otherwise
findings.impact: a wrong holdout number in a stored record

findings.defect: a daily capacity was silently ignored
findings.scenario: ten a day with no rows-per-day figure: 548 of 2000 rows chosen, the cap said not to bind; with a share too, the looser cap won
findings.cause: the daily cap needed rows a day and fell away without them; the share took precedence
findings.fix: a daily cap without rows a day is refused; with both, the tighter holds
findings.impact: more actions than the team can take

findings.defect: the holdout could act on more rows than the capacity
findings.scenario: a capacity of 10%, one action on ten training rows, a holdout of fifteen: two actions where one was allowed
findings.cause: the holdout count was a rounded share with at least one
findings.fix: the holdout applies the chosen threshold, then the capacity's floor
findings.impact: a holdout number for a decision the team could not take

findings.defect: under a binding capacity the holdout acted on too few rows
findings.scenario: the delivery-fraud replica through the engine with a review decision (seed 1): the team could review 16 rides; the threshold carried from the out-of-fold scores picked 6, found 1 of 13 frauds and realised far below its interval
findings.cause: the holdout and the interval's draws read the decision as a threshold; when the capacity ends the list, that threshold is only where the capacity fell on the training rows, and rows scored on another scale (unseen bikers) fall under it
findings.fix: a binding capacity is applied as a quota: the highest-ranked rows the capacity allows, each still worth acting on alone, in the draws and on the holdout; the result says how it was applied
findings.impact: a review team told to check fewer cases than it can, and a value far below its promise
alternatives: keep the threshold and widen the interval (hides the cause)

findings.defect: the fraud campaign could not test the choice and kept no ledger
findings.scenario: a review costing 2 against fares of about 250,000: the capacity bound on every seed and the cost never moved the share; each seed's folder held stages and activity but no ledger or session log; the code hash covered five files; a routed model in the owner's workspace could have answered
findings.cause: the campaign was written before its review
findings.fix: a review costs 25,000 (a tenth of a typical fare); each seed keeps its own ledger and session log under agent_runs and the rules decide (campaign_capture.recorded); the code hash covers the engine's folders whole; the decision file is written once
findings.impact: a gate that could not fail and records the store never saw

findings.defect: the quota's worth filter was stricter than the training's own choice
findings.scenario: low probabilities (scores times 0.3), a review worth 100 costing 20, capacity 2%: the point value lay outside its own interval and the holdout acted on 23 of the 60 allowed
findings.cause: the draws and the holdout kept only rows worth acting on alone, while the training's choice counted every row ranked at least as high as its threshold
findings.fix: a row is kept when it is worth acting on alone or ranked as high as the rows chosen
findings.impact: an interval that excluded its own point and an under-filled quota

findings.defect: a tie across the capacity made the core say no action pays
findings.scenario: the top 50 rows tied at 0.9 with a capacity of 10 rows; tree models' rounded scores at 0.5% did it in 22 of 50 seeds
findings.cause: a list may end only where the rank changes, so under the capacity the only allowed count was none
findings.fix: the capacity itself may end the list inside a tie
findings.impact: a team told to review nothing when its best cases tie

findings.defect: the fraud campaign built its project before recording began
findings.scenario: seed 0: the ledger held 32 decisions but no target, task, identifier, group or time decision, and no benchmark label from the planted traps
findings.cause: the build ran outside the recorded block, and the replica's labels were never written
findings.fix: the build inside the recorded block, and the replica's traps label the decisions after the run
findings.impact: the decisions most worth training on, missing from the store

findings.defect: a capacity per day is applied as one pool over the holdout
findings.scenario: a quota from a daily capacity ranks rows across every holdout day at once
findings.cause: the core is not told each row's day
findings.fix: said in applied_as; filling day by day is left open
findings.impact: one day may take many days' reviews in the reading
alternatives: pass each holdout row's day and fill the quota day by day
findings.open: fill a daily capacity day by day

findings.defect: the fraud campaign's coverage miss was first read as an interval too narrow, which seven seeds cannot show
findings.scenario: fraud_decision_v1: 5 of 7 seeds inside a 90% interval, one below and one above
findings.cause: 5 of 7 or fewer happens about 15 times in 100 under a right 90% interval; v1's misses in units of the interval have a root mean square of 1.23 with a 90% interval of 0.86 to 2.2; a simulation of fraud-like data found 87 to 93% coverage but leaves out the engine's model choice, which can shift the centre
findings.fix: measured on 30 fresh seeds (fraud_decision_v2): coverage 0.86 and centre pass, width fails (root mean square of z 1.29, 90% interval 1.06 to 1.64): the interval is too narrow by about a quarter; the holdout-sized entity bootstrap, fixed before the run as the next step, follows
findings.impact: a wider interval without evidence would hide a shifted centre, the likelier fault
alternatives: widen it at once (as first proposed): rejected on the simulation
findings.open: the holdout-sized entity bootstrap, measured as fraud_decision_v3

findings.defect: v2's first design could pass a wrong interval
findings.scenario: a seed that chose to act but acted on no holdout row left the count (23 of 28 passing where 23 of 30 should fail); an inside-or-outside count passes an interval a fifth too narrow about half the time and a shifted centre about nine times in ten
findings.cause: the gate read only how often the result landed inside
findings.fix: every seed that chose to act counts; each miss is measured in units of its interval (z) with its side; the mean of z (centre) and the root mean square of z (width) are gated, the next step fixed before the run; fewer than 20 acting is inconclusive
findings.impact: a measurement that could not answer its own question
alternatives: gate the expected value's interval too (a confidence interval for the average, not a promise about one holdout: rejected)

findings.defect: v2's report crashed writing its verdict
findings.scenario: thirty seeds done, the verdict file never written
findings.cause: a gate's comparison with a chi-squared quantile gave a numpy bool, which JSON does not write
findings.fix: plain bools and floats in the verdict; the verdict written again from the thirty saved results
findings.impact: a finished measurement without its verdict

findings.defect: the first holdout-sized bootstrap passed for the wrong reason
findings.scenario: on v2's own seeds it held 25 of 29 with misses of the right size, but its samples were a third smaller than the holdout: about 150 rides without a biker each counted as an entity in training, and a sample of the holdout's count of entities drew many of them
findings.cause: samples sized by a count of entities, which rows with no entity and skewed entity sizes distort
findings.fix: samples sized by the holdout's rows, whole entities drawn until the rows are reached; an entity's size looked up by its code (rows with no entity have codes past the others: the first version crashed there, now tested)
findings.impact: an interval that looked fixed by measuring the wrong sample
alternatives: count only named entities (still mis-sized when sizes are skewed)

findings.defect: on a time split with entities the samples were several times too large
findings.scenario: the holdout's entities are new and have a few rows each; their count of full-history training entities held many more rows
findings.impact: an interval narrower than before on time-and-entity splits

findings.defect: sized right, the interval was still too narrow on v2's seeds
findings.scenario: row-sized samples: 24 of 29 inside, misses 1.24 times its size
findings.cause: likely the final model's own ranking: the holdout is scored by one model, a dozen reviews deep, while the training rows were scored by five fold models whose quirks average out
findings.fix: each sample drawn from one fold's rows (one model's ranking); explored on v2's own seeds: 26 of 29 inside, misses 1.01 times its size; the verdict is fraud_decision_v3's on fresh seeds
findings.impact: a range a quarter narrower than the decision's real uncertainty
alternatives: calibrate the half-width by a measured factor (empirical, no mechanism)

findings.defect: the training intervals moved when a holdout was passed
findings.scenario: the inner samples drew from the same random stream as the training draws
findings.fix: the inner samples have their own stream
findings.impact: two runs on the same rows disagreeing for no reason

findings.defect: the one-fold samples picked a fold by entity, could fall short, and suit no time split
findings.scenario: the replica's riderless rides, one group in its folds but 156 entities in the bootstrap, made their fold come up about twice as often; a fold of a few entities could not fill a holdout-sized sample; a time split's first fold model is its weakest
findings.cause: a fold drawn from the list of entities; a fixed number of picks; folds passed for every split
findings.fix: a fold by a random row; picks drawn on until the rows are reached; no folds on time splits; the docstring says what folds assume; v3's width gate catches an interval too wide as well as too narrow
findings.impact: an interval sized by one fold too often, or too wide where the models do not differ

measurements.name: interval coverage in simulation (60 seeds, 3000 rows each, 90% nominal)
measurements.gate: each interval holds what it says about nine times in ten
measurements.result: the expected value's interval held the true value 57 of 60; the prediction interval held the holdout 54 of 60
measurements.next: measure on the delivery_fraud replica through the engine in 34.4

measurements.name: fraud_decision_v1: a review decision through the engine on 8 seeds of the delivery-fraud replica (a fraud caught saves the ride's fare, a review costs 25,000, at most 0.5% of rides)
measurements.gate: pass when all three hold: chosen on every seed; never more holdout actions than the capacity allows; the realised value per ride inside its 90% prediction interval on at least 6 of 8 seeds
measurements.result: 7 seeds acted, each as a quota and within its capacity; on seed 5 the selected model's scores made no review pay, so it acted on nothing; the realised value fell inside its interval on 5 of the 7 that acted (seed 1 below: 177.9 against 381.5 to 1747.7; seed 3 above: 1093.6 against 259.2 to 1033.8)
measurements.next: measure the interval on 30 fresh seeds (fraud_decision_v2) before changing it: a simulation of fraud-like data found 87 to 93% coverage
measurements.against_gate: The coverage gate fails (5 inside, 6 needed); the capacity gate fails only because seed 5 acted on nothing and so had no reading, a flaw of the gate as written, not an excess.
limits: partial labels: both values are lower bounds of the same kind
the interval's misses go both ways (one below, one above), so no bias in one direction is shown

measurements.name: fraud_decision_v2: the review decision's 90% prediction interval through the engine on 30 fresh seeds (8 to 37) of the delivery-fraud replica
measurements.gate: pass when all hold: chosen on every seed; capacity kept on every seed that acted; at least 80% of the seeds that acted inside their interval (at least 20 acting); the mean of z within 1.645 / sqrt(N); the 90% chi-squared interval of the root mean square of z reaching down to 1
measurements.result: 29 seeds acted, all within capacity; 25 inside (0.8621); misses 1 below, 3 above; mean z 0.0483 (bound 0.3055); root mean square of z 1.2854 with a 90% interval of 1.0611 to 1.6449
measurements.next: a holdout-sized entity bootstrap, as fixed before the run: draw the holdout's number of entities in each bootstrap draw, apply the decision as it runs, read the quantiles
measurements.against_gate: Coverage and centre pass; the width gate fails: the misses are larger than the interval says, by about a quarter, on both sides.
limits: the report's verdict file was written after the run by a fixed report (a numpy bool crashed it); the thirty results are as the run wrote them

outcome: DCLab has one decision core: a person's values, costs and capacity give the operating point with the highest expected value, its tested intervals and the holdout read once; the review budget and the stated-cost threshold are its special cases.
lessons: Test an interval for what it means: a confidence interval for an average is not a promise about one new sample.
A threshold acts on ties together; a search over counts must too.
Before fixing a miss, ask how often the miss happens by chance: 5 of 7 inside a 90% interval happens about one time in seven when the interval is right.
risks: the engine's review path still uses review_budget until 34.4
the delivery_fraud and delivery_time replicas not yet measured through the engine
